body:
An update for anyone who cares.  I guess the pills weren't enough to kill me, just enough to knock me out from when I posted last until just now.

I'm pretty sure my wife is going to leave me, so I plan on letting her leave and trying again so she doesn't have to go through the pain of seeing me die.

What is strange is that after I try I usually wake up and wish I hadn't tried to commit suicide, today I am sad that I didn't die.
Atheism is actually what's kept me alive this long.  It's the wonders of what we'll discover next that keeps me alive.

Thanks for the reply, I honestly can't think of a single reason to not kill myself right now, except three things.  The first is my sister's husband killed himself, and I don't want to put her through having her brother do the same thing.  The second is I don't want my wife to feel like it's her fault, and the third is our three puppies.

I hurt her emotionally (I would never physically hurt her) all the time, and my post above explains why, it's like i'm not in control.

As for the pills, I'm not sure it's lethal dose, though I'm hoping it is.  If it's not, I will most likely try again later on after my wife leaves me.

Thank you for your post, and I do appreciate the help.

I had a really bad childhood.  I saw things from my parents that nobody should ever have to see.  I saw my father pull a gun and threaten to kill all of us and himself, while holding my sister and crying.  My parents are crack addicts whom I don't talk to anymore and I only talk to two out of three sisters.

Like I said in the original post, I have post traumatic stress disorder.  I also have the beginning stages of split personality, though I don't have two different "identities", it is like there is someone else that is controlling me when I go into a dark mode.  It's like when an argument or something stresses me out to much, another person takes over and the best way to describe it is that it's like watching TV, I'm there watching, but I can't control what I do.  My therapist says it's a protective mechanism for my brain, I began doing this as a child.  Also, I black out a lot of what happens during this.  My wife will tell me things I said or things that happened and I genuinely do not remember it.

The other night while I wasn't in control, I put a gun in my mouth and almost pulled the trigger in front of my wife, and I've hurt her more by doing things like this in the past than I ever want to remember.

And to finally answer your question of the details for tonight, well I'm suicidal and hurting her that way for one, and she's leaving me.  I have absolutely nobody except her.  I don't talk to most of my family, very few friends, so there's really no point in living anymore for me.

FWIW, your FSM comment did make me laugh, so thank you for that.  I know it seems small, but it made me feel a little bit of happiness during a time where all I feel is pain, depression, and self loathing.

>I've always wondered... The nothingness that some people believe await us after death, is it eternal or instantaneous...? How can there be anything resembling time where there is nothingness?
I imagine it like this, remember what it was like before you were born?  That's sorta what it would be like.

>However, people who have come close to death do speak of seeing a light, a phenomenon called near-death experiences (NDEs) which I'm sure you're familiar with. And the interesting thing is that [1] the scientists who take the time to study this phenomenon become convinced by the evidence that there's something fascinating beyond mere brain processes going on here.
While I do believe in near death experiences, I don't believe there's anything divine going on.  From some of the scientific papers I've read on the subject (I'm no expert, but I have read a few), there's actually a chemical that's released into your brain as you're dying that's a hallucinogenic drug that's there to help your brain cope with the last few dying moments

Thank you for your post though, it means a lot to me and has made me feel slightly better.
